title: Declarative indicators by default and explicit trust for Python
context: AI-authored indicators need inspectable behavior and bounded execution without claiming a child process is a secure sandbox.
decision: Use validated declarative indicators by default; trusted Python execution remains an explicitly authorized capability.
consequences: Indicator previews require validation, resource limits and isolation from accepted state.
Every trusted Python execution needs the existing operation-specific confirmation.
history_note: Common record metadata was added when repository continuity was established. The existing trust boundary is preserved.
default: declarative AST, validated structured output, no eval or exec
python: Disabled by default. Every trusted-code execution needs user authorization bound to code, inputs and revision.
isolation_claim: A child process and resource limits are not a secure sandbox.
m0: Protocol runtime only. No indicator source execution or SDK credentials.
revisit_when: Reliable OS isolation has been implemented and independently validated.
